title: An MCP client connects to a protected server

story.title: The client tried to connect
story.what: The MCP client sent initialize without a token.
story.why: It doesn't yet know this server needs authorization.
story.matters: Discovery starts from a plain request; nothing is preconfigured.

story.title: The server challenged it
story.what: The server answered 401 with a pointer to its protected-resource metadata.
story.why: RFC 9728 lets a resource advertise which authorization server protects it.
story.matters: If a server skips this challenge, discovery-driven clients never start the auth flow.

story.title: The client registered itself
story.what: The client registered dynamically and received a client_id.
story.why: Agents meet servers at runtime; pre-registration doesn't scale.
story.matters: The authorization server still decides which redirect URIs and grants it allows.

story.title: You signed in and approved
story.what: You authenticated at the authorization server and consented to the client's access.
story.why: The agent acts with your identity, so you authorize it.
story.matters: The agent never handles your credentials.

story.title: The client connected with a token
story.what: The MCP server accepted the token and listed its tools.
story.why: The token's audience is this server (RFC 8707 resource indicator).
story.matters: One server's token can't be replayed against another.

subtitle: MCP authorization: RFC 9728 discovery, dynamic client registration, auth code + PKCE

outcome.detail: Discovery, registration and sign-in completed; the client holds a token for this MCP server only.
outcome.caption: challenge → discovery → DCR → auth code → token · tools listed
